persona.name: Alex Rivera
persona.description: Synthetic final-year CS student / software engineer. All facts are fictional and authored by us for reproducible evaluation; no real user data is used.

messages.content: I'm setting up a new laptop. For context, I always code in VS Code with dark mode on, and for machine learning work I strongly prefer Python over everything else.
Got it. I'll assume VS Code with a dark theme, and Python as your go-to for ML.
Right. I also dislike verbose inline comments, I'd rather keep code self-explanatory.
Quick note about me: I'm vegetarian and I'm allergic to peanuts, so keep that in mind for any recipe suggestions.
Understood, vegetarian and peanut allergy noted.
Also every morning I go for a run and then grab an oat milk latte.
My final-year project is called UniMemory, a long-term memory layer for AI apps. The backend is built with FastAPI and uses PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension for vector search.
Nice, FastAPI + Postgres/pgvector is a solid stack for that.
The hard deadline for the final evaluation is in November.
On the side I'm building an expense-splitting app for friends called TripSplit. It's a React Native app.
Expense splitting in React Native, sounds handy for group trips.
Yeah but I'm currently stuck on the authentication flow.
I live in Mumbai now, but I'm originally from Pune. I'm a final-year student at Somaiya.
Mumbai-based, Pune roots, studying at Somaiya, got it.
I have a younger sister named Nisha.
My girlfriend's name is Maya. Our anniversary is March 12.
Maya, anniversary on March 12, noted.
She loves sunflowers, I always get her those.
I'm planning a trip to Goa from December 20 to 26 with my college friends.
Goa, Dec 20-26, with college friends, sounds fun.
Need to book the flights soon.
I'm giving a talk at PyCon in October about vector search for memory systems.
A PyCon talk on vector search, that's a great topic.
I still need to finish the slides.
Next I want to learn Rust, I keep hearing good things about it.
Rust is a great next step, especially coming from Python.
Right now I'm reading Designing Data-Intensive Applications.
I have a cat named Pixel who wakes me up at 6am every day.
Pixel the cat, 6am wake-up, noted.
I drive a blue Honda City to campus.
